messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran into a nasty edge during the sample-app onboarding. When a stream is interrupted mid-logical-message the client sometimes ends up with a duplicated tail fragment or a missing suffix and the JSON parser chokes. Repro below.

ben: Oof. Browser EventSource or node fetch stream? Short repro please.

maria: Both. Browser EventSource and node-stream sample. Repro steps: 1) start a stream that emits logical JSON messages split into multiple chunks 2) force a network drop in the middle of a logical message 3) client reconnects with Last-Event-ID and occasionally receives fragments that duplicate or drop the trailing bytes.

sam: Any console/server traces? Sounds like resume semantics mismatch (fragment vs logical message).

maria: Client trace (trimmed):

received chunk id=10 data=\"{\\\"role\\\":\\\"assistant\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Hel\"}\nreceived chunk id=11 data=\"{\\\"role\\\":\\\"assistant\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"lo, wo\"}\n// network drop here
reconnect Last-Event-ID=11
received chunk id=11 data=\"rld\\\"\nreceived chunk id=12 data=\"{\\\"role\\\":\\\"assistant\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Bye\\\"}\n
maria: Depending on timing the client ends up concatenating 11+11', or merging 11' with 12, producing invalid JSON or duplicated text.

ben: This implies the server is advancing the Last-Event-ID at fragment emission. We should only advance on the completion of a logical message. Can't rely on chunk boundaries.

sam: On runtime we currently stream tokenizer/kernel outputs as fragments. Two options: 1) server-side: emit an explicit logical-boundary sentinel when a full message is finished (e.g., a comment line like ":boundary <token>") or publish resume tokens that map to logical messages; 2) client-side: add reassembly/dedupe heuristics.

maria: For a quick fix I implemented conservative reassembly in the sample-apps: store the last-fragment SHA1 per event-id and drop duplicates on resume. It's ugly but stabilizes the onboarding experience across JS/Python/Go samples. Note: Go sample was the worst because it tried to parse every incoming chunk immediately.

ben: Add an explicit note in the SDK Quickstart and the sample-app README explaining parity differences. We don't want users to copy the hack into production, so make it conspicuous.

ci-bot: test job queued: sample-app/stream-flap -> headless (job 9991) :spiral_calendar:

maria: Also added a tiny test harness (sample-app/tests/stream-flap.test.js) that toggles the host network using puppeteer to reproduce the flap locally and in CI. Hooked it behind an env flag to avoid flakiness by default.

sam: Please open a runtime ticket with attached traces and a proposal for an atomic flush/resume design. If runtime prefers sentinel lines, we need a backwards-compatible plan and a migration window.

maria: Filed TKT-3499: "streaming: resume tokens should represent logical-message boundaries; avoid advancing on raw fragment emission". Attached client traces and a short compatibility plan.

ben: Reviewed the sample-app PR — looks good. Add an inline comment in the reassembly helper explaining the dedupe rationale and link to TKT-3499. Also add a short note in release notes when the runtime change lands so we can remove the workaround.

ci-bot: CI passed: sample-app (branch: fix/stream-resume-dedupe) :white_check_mark:

maria: Pushed the comment, README blurb, and the test harness. Leaving follow-up for runtime and cross-SDK interop tests.

sam: Created follow-up TKT-3504 to add node/python/go/mobile interop streaming tests in CI once runtime emits a migration ETA.

maria: Thanks — flagging this thread for follow-up when runtime ETA is available. :thumbsup:
